Rashi on Menachot 94a:11:1.hebrew: דפוס - פורמ"א בלע"ז, ובגמ' מפרש היאך עשוי:
Rashi on Menachot 94a:11:1.english: A mold - Forme in Old French; and in the Gemara it explains how it was made.

Rashi on Menachot 94a:11:2.english: And when he removes [them] - From the oven.

Rashi on Menachot 94a:11:3.english: He places them in a mold - So that they will not become damaged and break.

Rashi on Menachot 94a:12:1.english: The one loaf - It is written with regard to the showbread.

Rashi on Menachot 94a:13:1.hebrew: ושמת אותם - שימה ראשונה שאתה עושה מהם, דהיינו בתנור, תהא בלשון אותם, דמשמע שהיה נותן שתים בשני דפוסין יחד בתנור:
Rashi on Menachot 94a:13:1.english: And you shall set them - The first placement that you make of them, that is, in the oven, is [indicated by] the expression “them,” which implies that he would place two [loaves] in two molds together into the oven.

Rashi on Menachot 94a:15:1.hebrew: ועדיין היא בצק - נותנה בדפוס, שהדפוס עשוי כמין תיבה פרוצה, ולמר כמין ספינה רוקדת, כדפליגי לקמן. ומתקן הבצק בתוך הדפוס, שיהא עשוי כעין הדפוס, שהלחם היה לו דפנות ותוך:
Rashi on Menachot 94a:15:1.english: While it is still dough - He places it into a mold, for the mold is shaped like an open box, and according to the [other] Master, like a rocking ship, as they dispute below. And he arranges the dough inside the mold so that it will be formed like the mold, for the bread had sides and an interior.

Rashi on Menachot 94a:15:2.hebrew: וכמין דפוס היה לה בתנור - והיו מסיקין אותו עם התנור, ואופה את הלחם:
Rashi on Menachot 94a:15:2.english: And there was a type of mold for it in the oven - And they would heat it along with the oven, and he would bake the bread [in it].

Rashi on Menachot 94a:15:3.english: And when he removes it - From the oven.

Rashi on Menachot 94a:15:4.hebrew: וליהדרה - לאחר שרדה, לדפוס קמא שתקנה בו:
Rashi on Menachot 94a:15:4.english: And let him return it - After he removed it [from the oven], to the first mold in which he shaped it.

Rashi on Menachot 94a:15:5.english: It swelled - And it requires a mold larger than the first.

Rashi on Menachot 94a:1:1.english: With live and with slaughtered [offerings] - In the case of the lambs of Atzeret [Shavuot].

Rashi on Menachot 94a:1:2.english: And in an item that has no living spirit - Bread and meal-offerings.

Rashi on Menachot 94a:1:3.hebrew: מה שאין כן בסמיכה - דאין נוהגין בשחוטין, ואין נוהג אלא בדבר שיש בו רוח חיים:
Rashi on Menachot 94a:1:3.english: Which is not the case with semikhah - For it is not practiced on slaughtered [animals], and it applies only to that which has the breath of life.

Rashi on Menachot 94a:3:1.hebrew: שיכול - שיהא האחד סומך לכל החבירים, והלא דין הוא וכו':
Rashi on Menachot 94a:3:1.english: For one might [think] - That one [partner] should place his hands on behalf of all the partners; "and is it not a logical deduction, etc.?"

Rashi on Menachot 94a:3:3.hebrew: נתמעטה בחוברין - שאין כולם צריכין להניף, אלא אחד מניף על יד כולם:
Rashi on Menachot 94a:3:3.english: Was diminished regarding partners - That not all of them are required to wave; rather, one waves on behalf of all of them.

Rashi on Menachot 94a:4:1.english: And let waving be extended to partners - That all of them should be required to wave.

Rashi on Menachot 94a:4:2.hebrew: תנופה שנתרבית בשחוטין - בין בשלמי צבור, בין בשלמי יחיד:
Rashi on Menachot 94a:4:2.english: Waving, which was extended to slaughtered offerings - Both in communal peace offerings and in individual peace offerings.

Rashi on Menachot 94a:5:1.hebrew: קא הוי חציצה - דכי מניף זה ידו ע"י חבירו, הויא ידו חוצצת בין יד חבירו לזבח:
Rashi on Menachot 94a:5:1.english: There is an interposition - For when this one waves his hand on top of his fellow's hand, his hand constitutes an interposition between his fellow's hand and the sacrifice.

Rashi on Menachot 94a:5:2.english: Let him wave - One [partner should wave], and then his fellow should wave.

Rashi on Menachot 94a:5:3.hebrew: תנופה - אחת כתיב, אבל בסמיכה לא כתיב סמיכה בהדיא, אלא וסמך סתם, [יכול] לסמוך והדר לסמוך:
Rashi on Menachot 94a:5:3.english: Waving - One [waving] is written. But regarding leaning, "leaning" is not written explicitly, but rather simply "and he shall lean" — [so one can] lean and then [another can] lean.

Rashi on Menachot 94a:6:1.english: And brought him up - [The deputy brought up] the High Priest.

Rashi on Menachot 94a:6:2.hebrew: הושיט הראשון - מאותן י"ב שעסוקים בתמיד, וסומך עליהם כהן גדול וזורקן על האישים. ונשמט השני והלך לו, ובא חבירו שלישי ומושיט לראשון, והראשון לכהן גדול:
Rashi on Menachot 94a:6:2.english: The first held out - [One] of those twelve who are engaged with the daily offering, and the High Priest places his hands upon them and throws them onto the altar fires. And the second slips away and departs, and his fellow, the third, comes and hands [the limbs] to the first, and the first to the High Priest.

Rashi on Menachot 94a:9:1.hebrew: משום יקרא דכהן גדול - שיהא נראה כמו שהקריב הוא את כולן, היה סומך עליהן, ולא שתהא סמיכתם נוהגת בשחוטין מן התורה:
Rashi on Menachot 94a:9:1.english: Because of the honor of the High Priest - So that it would appear as though he had offered all of them [himself], he would lean upon them, and not that leaning applies to slaughtered [offerings] by Torah law.

Tosafot on Menachot 94a:11:1.hebrew: שתי הלחם - במשנה ובמקרא קרוי לשון זכר ולשון נקבה, דהכא תנן: שתי הלחם, ובשמואל (א י) כתיב גבי שאול: ונתנו לך שתי לחם ולקחת מידם; ולעיל פ' ואלו מנחות (מנחות דף עה:) קרי ליה לשון זכר, דקאמר: בבא מלחם גדול, וכתיב (ישעיהו נ״א:י״ד): ולא יחסר לחמו:
Tosafot on Menachot 94a:11:1.english: The two loaves - In [both] the Mishnah and Scripture, [the word *lechem*, bread,] is treated as both masculine and feminine. For here we learned [in the feminine]: "The two loaves" [using the feminine numeral *shtei*]; and in Samuel (I 10:4) it is written regarding Saul: "and they will give you two loaves of bread, and you shall take [them] from their hand" [also using *shtei*]; and earlier, in the chapter "Elu Menachot" (Menachot 75b), it refers to it in the masculine gender, as it says: "when it comes from a large loaf" [using the masculine adjective *gadol*]; and it is written (Isaiah 51:14): "nor will his bread fail" [using the masculine verb *yechsar*].

Tosafot on Menachot 94a:11:2.hebrew: ובדפוס היה עושה אותן - אית דגרסי טפוס, והכל אחד, כמו גיטין (דף כו.) טופסי גיטין, פורמ"א בלע"ז. ואי אפשר לברר אם היה מתקן הלחם מחוץ לדפוס, שהיה הדפוס בתוך הלחם, או הלחם בפנים. ומתוך הסברא נראה שהלחם בתוך הדפוס. אבל מדקאמר בגמ' "וליהדרה בדפוס קמא", ומשני: "כיון דאפי לה נפחה", משמע שהלחם חוץ לדפוס; דאי בתוך הדפוס, כיון דכמין דפוס היה לה בתנור, היכי מינפחה? הא אין הדפוס מניחה! ועוד, דבכל דוכתא משמע שהיו מדביקין את הפת בתנור, ואם בתוך הדפוס נתונה, אי אפשר להדביקה. ומהא דקתני "וכשהוא רודן נותנן בדפוס", אין לדקדק, דשייך רדיה מפני הדפוס, ולא מפני שהודבקה בתנור:
Tosafot on Menachot 94a:11:2.english: And in a mold he would make them - Some have the textual reading tefus [with a tet], but it is all one [and the same], as in Gittin (26a), "blank formulas of bills of divorce" [tofsei gittin], forme in Old French. And it is impossible to clarify [with certainty] whether he would prepare the bread on the outside of the mold, such that the mold was inside the bread, or [whether] the bread was on the inside [of the mold]. Based on logical reasoning, it would seem that the bread was inside the mold. However, from the fact that the Gemara says: "And let him return it to the first mold!" and answers: "Once it baked, it swelled" — this implies that the bread was on the outside of the mold. For if it were inside the mold, since it had a mold-like form in the oven, how could it swell? Surely the mold would not allow it! Furthermore, everywhere it implies that they would stick the bread to [the walls of] the oven, and if it were placed inside the mold, it would be impossible to stick it. And from that which is taught [in the Mishnah], "and when he removes them, he places them in a mold," one cannot infer [that it was stuck to the oven wall], for the term "removal" [rediyyah] can apply on account of [removing it from] the mold, and not [necessarily] because it was stuck to the oven.

Tosafot on Menachot 94a:11:3.hebrew: וכשהוא רודן נותנן בדפוס - הן הקערות של שולחן, כדאמר (לקמן מנחות דף צז.): "קערותיו - אלו דפוסין", וכן פירש רש"י בפירושי חומש שהיה נותנו בקערות לאחר אפייה. ותימה: הא דפליגי לקמן (מנחות דף צה:) באפייתן אי דחיא שבת - דלמאן דאמר תנור מקדש דחיא שבת, משום דאי אפי לה מאתמול איפסלא בלינה, ולמאן דאמר אין תנור מקדש לא דחיא - הא בין למר ובין למר קערות נתקדשו, כדכתיב בפ' נשא: "ומשחת בו את אהל מועד ואת ארון העדות, את השולחן ואת כל כליו"! ושמא אע"ג דכתיב גבי שלחן "ועשית קערותיו", מ"מ כלי השולחן מיהא לא מיקרו. אי נמי, מאן דמפרש "קערותיו - אלו הדפוסים" קסבר תנור מקדש; אבל מאן דאמר אין תנור מקדש, היה מפרש דקערותיו היינו קערות שהיו נותנים בהם את הלחם על שתי שולחנות שבאולם, אחד מכסף ואחד מזהב: על של כסף נותנים לחם הפנים בכניסתן, ועל של זהב ביציאתן. אבל אין לפרש דעל שולחן של משה שבהיכל היו סודרין בתוך הקערות, דאם כן שולחן היה מקדש יותר מחמשה עשר טפחים:
Tosafot on Menachot 94a:11:3.english: And when he removes them [from the oven], he places them in a mold - These are the bowls (ke’arot) of the Table, as [the Gemara] says below (Menachot 97a): “'Its bowls' — these are the molds.” And Rashi similarly explained in his commentary on the Torah that one would place it into the bowls after baking. And this is difficult: regarding the dispute below (Menachot 95b) as to whether their baking overrides Shabbat — where according to the one who says the oven sanctifies, it overrides Shabbat, because if one baked it yesterday [on Friday] it would be disqualified by remaining overnight (linah); and according to the one who says the oven does not sanctify, it does not override [Shabbat] — yet according to both authorities, the bowls were sanctified [as sacred vessels], as it is written in Parashat Naso [Exodus 30:26–27]: “And with it you shall anoint the Tent of Meeting and the Ark of the Testimony, the Table and all its vessels”! [Thus, placing the bread in the mold on Friday should likewise sanctify it and subject it to disqualification by remaining overnight!] And perhaps even though it is written regarding the Table, “And you shall make its bowls” [Exodus 25:29], nevertheless they are at least not considered “the Table's vessels” [that were consecrated to sanctify what is placed inside them]. Alternatively, the one who explains “'its bowls' — these are the molds” holds that the oven sanctifies. But the one who says the oven does not sanctify would explain that “its bowls” were bowls in which they would place the bread upon the two tables that were in the Vestibule (Ulam) — one of silver and one of gold: upon the silver one they would place the showbread upon its entrance, and upon the golden one upon its departure. However, one cannot explain that they would arrange [the loaves] inside the bowls upon Moses' Table in the Sanctuary (Heikhal), for if so, the Table would [have had to] sanctify higher than fifteen handbreadths.

Tosafot on Menachot 94a:15:1.hebrew: ושמת אותם בדפוס - וא"ת: והא אפיקתיה לומר שאפייתן שתים שתים? ויש לומר: דאם כן, לכתוב "ונתת אותם", אבל "ושמת" משמע שימה בדפוס:
Tosafot on Menachot 94a:15:1.english: And you shall place them in a mold - And if you say: But surely you already applied it to teach that their baking is two by two? One can say: For if so, let [the verse] write, "And you shall put them" [venatata otam]; but "and you shall place them" [vesamta] implies placement in a mold.

Tosafot on Menachot 94a:3:1.hebrew: סמיכה שלא נתרבתה בשחוטין - תימה, ותתרבה בשחוטין מקל וחומר מתנופה, שנתמעטה בחוברין ונתרבתה בשחוטין:
Tosafot on Menachot 94a:3:1.english: Semikhah, which was not extended to slaughtered animals - This is puzzling: why should [semikhah] not be extended to slaughtered animals via an a fortiori argument (kal va-chomer) from waving, which was excluded in the case of partners and yet extended to slaughtered animals [so semikhah, which applies to partners, should all the more so apply to slaughtered animals]?

Tosafot on Menachot 94a:5:1.hebrew: קא הויא חציצה - והא דכהן מניח ידו תחת יד הבעלים ומניף, פירשתי לעיל בפרק כל המנחות באות מצה (מנחות דף סא:):
Tosafot on Menachot 94a:5:1.english: It constitutes an interposition - And as for that which a priest places his hand beneath the owner's hand and waves, I explained [this] above in the chapter "All Meal-Offerings Come as Matzah" (Menachot 61b).

Tosafot on Menachot 94a:6:1.english: When the High Priest wishes to burn [the offerings] - This is a mishna in tractate Tamid (33b).
